skills.title: Add configurable line endings at the shared file-write boundary
skills.summary: Expose a constrained platform/LF/CRLF output option, propagate the selected mode from application startup into the shared I/O service, translate it to the text-runtime newline value, and apply it when opening files for writing so all existing centralized write callers inherit the policy.

ordered_actions.action: Define a user-facing line-ending option restricted to platform, LF, and CRLF, retaining platform behavior as the compatibility default.
Pass the parsed line-ending mode from application startup into the shared file I/O component.
Map platform, LF, and CRLF modes to the text I/O newline arguments null, "\n", and "\r\n".
Provide the mapped newline value to the centralized text-file open operation so existing writers use the selected convention without caller-specific changes.

preconditions: Application output files are written through a shared text I/O service.
The text I/O runtime supports an explicit newline parameter.
Application startup can pass parsed configuration into the shared I/O service.
outcomes: Users can select platform-native, LF, or CRLF line endings for file writes.
The default preserves prior platform-dependent behavior.
Coder edits and other callers of the shared write method inherit the configured policy.
exclusions: Does not independently modify each file-writing caller.
Does not establish behavior for write paths that bypass the shared write method.
Does not include dedicated automated verification of emitted bytes or configuration-file parsing.

skills.title: Make Exact Text Edits Independent of Line-Ending Encoding
skills.summary: Orchestrate exact text editing by detecting the source file's newline convention, canonicalizing the file content and edit operands to LF, performing existence checks, uniqueness validation, no-op detection, indexing, and replacement on the canonical text, generating the semantic diff from canonical pre-edit and post-edit content, and restoring the detected newline convention only when writing the completed file.
preconditions: The operation performs an exact text replacement against file content.
Equivalent CRLF and LF sequences should be treated as the same text for matching.
The source file's selected LF or CRLF convention should be preserved after editing.

case_actions.action: Detect and retain the source file's newline convention before transforming its content.
Normalize the file content, search text, and replacement text to LF.
Run existence checks and occurrence counting on the normalized content, rejecting absent or non-unique matches as required.
Perform no-op comparison, index lookup, and replacement entirely in the normalized representation.
Generate the user-facing diff from normalized pre-edit and post-edit content so newline encoding does not inflate the apparent change.
Convert the completed normalized content back to the detected source convention and persist it.

failure_modes: Matching raw file content against model-provided text treats equivalent CRLF and LF sequences as unequal.
Checking uniqueness before canonicalization can miss logically duplicate matches encoded with different newline sequences.
Writing canonical LF content directly can unintentionally change a CRLF file's newline convention.
Generating diffs from differently encoded raw text can obscure or inflate the semantic edit.

Neither workflow subsumes the other.

skills.title: Decode a native NUL-terminated UTF-16 string through a pointer-width variable
skills.summary: When an FFI returns a raw address for a NUL-terminated UTF-16 string, serialize the address into a buffer limited to sizeof(void*) and pass that pointer variable to the FFI library’s native UTF-16 decoder instead of creating an arbitrary fixed-size external-memory view and scanning it manually.
skills.applicability: FFI bindings where a native API returns a numeric address to a NUL-terminated UTF-16 allocation and the decoder expects a pointer variable.

skills.title: Preserve the original native address for allocator-matched release
skills.summary: Keep the raw address returned by a native API separate from the decoded string and pass that unchanged address to the API-mandated deallocator after decoding, while retaining surrounding resource cleanup in finally blocks.
skills.applicability: Native interop code where decoding dereferences an allocation that remains owned by a specific native allocator.

skills.title: Verify native pointer marshalling at four-byte and eight-byte widths
skills.summary: Test pointer serialization with nontrivial BigInt addresses at both 32-bit and 64-bit pointer widths, asserting the exact decoder input width and bytes as well as preservation of the original address passed to native deallocation.
skills.applicability: FFI code that converts numeric native addresses into pointer buffers and must remain correct across process architectures.

skills.title: Test real FFI string decoding over live native-compatible buffers
skills.summary: Use the real FFI decoder with test-owned buffers whose lifetime spans the synchronous dereference, and cover UTF-16 edge cases including BMP code units with zero low bytes, surrogate pairs, embedded NUL termination, and strings exceeding any removed fixed-size bound.
skills.applicability: FFI string-decoding changes whose correctness depends on native decoder behavior, memory lifetime, Unicode handling, and termination semantics.

skills.title: Replace a bounded native UTF-16 view with pointer-aware FFI decoding and ownership-safe cleanup
skills.summary: For an FFI API that returns an allocated NUL-terminated UTF-16 string address, trace the out-parameter and allocator contract, remove the arbitrary external-memory view and manual terminator scan, marshal the address through a variable sized to sizeof(void*), decode it with the FFI library's native UTF-16 decoder, preserve the unchanged address for the required deallocator, and validate the complete result path across pointer widths, Unicode edge cases, NUL termination, and strings beyond the former bound.
skills.case_workflow_goal: Eliminate truncation and unsafe bounded reads when converting an allocator-owned native UTF-16 result while preserving the native ownership and cleanup contract.

case_actions.action: Inspect the native out-parameter, pointer representation, string termination convention, and mandated deallocator; identify that the fixed external view does not represent the allocation's actual size.
Derive the process pointer width with the FFI library and serialize the returned BigInt address into a pointer variable restricted to that width.
Pass the pointer variable to the FFI library's NUL-terminated UTF-16 decoder, replacing the fixed-size external view and manual code-unit scan.
Keep the raw returned address distinct from the decoded text and release that unchanged address with the API-mandated deallocator while retaining surrounding resource cleanup in finally blocks.
Use fake-FFI tests at four-byte and eight-byte pointer widths to verify exact pointer-buffer bytes and width, decoder invocation, and preservation of the original deallocation address.

Exercise the production result path with the real FFI decoder over live test-owned buffers, covering BMP code units with zero low bytes, surrogate pairs, NUL termination, data longer than the removed 32 KiB bound, deallocation, and enclosing COM cleanup.

preconditions: The native API returns a raw address to a NUL-terminated UTF-16 allocation.
The FFI library can report sizeof(void*) and decode a UTF-16 string through a pointer variable.
The allocation must be released with a specific native deallocator after synchronous decoding.
The returned address can be represented without loss as a BigInt and serialized using the platform's native pointer width.

failure_modes.cause: Constructing a fixed-size external-memory view when the native allocation size is unknown.
failure_modes.effect: Long strings may be truncated, while the view may also describe memory beyond the actual allocation.

failure_modes.cause: Scanning UTF-16 bytes manually with an arbitrary upper bound.
failure_modes.effect: Termination and Unicode handling become coupled to an invalid size assumption.

failure_modes.cause: Serializing an address with the wrong pointer width or passing address bytes in the wrong pointer shape.
failure_modes.effect: The FFI decoder may dereference an incorrect address, especially when behavior differs between 32-bit and 64-bit processes.

failure_modes.cause: Overwriting or transforming the raw address during decoding.
failure_modes.effect: The mandated deallocator may receive a value other than the address returned by the owning API.

failure_modes.cause: Testing only mocked string results rather than a live-buffer dereference.
failure_modes.effect: Pointer marshalling, native decoding, buffer lifetime, NUL handling, and removal of the old size limit may remain unverified.

skills.applicability: Applicable to native bindings where an API returns an allocator-owned pointer to a NUL-terminated UTF-16 string and the FFI decoder expects a pointer variable rather than an arbitrarily sized external-memory view.
exclusions: Do not apply when the native API supplies an authoritative explicit byte or code-unit length that must govern decoding.
Do not apply when the returned data is not NUL-terminated UTF-16.
Do not replace asynchronous lifetime management with a test-owned buffer that expires before native dereference.
Do not infer the correct deallocator from the pointer type; follow the native API's ownership contract.

skills.title: Audit and route all runtime state through the configurable home
skills.summary: Audit the repository for runtime-state paths that bypass the canonical configurable-home resolver, replace hardcoded operating-system-home constructions across module-level constants and operational call sites with the shared or already-resolved runtime home while preserving the legacy fallback, then validate both state discovery and state creation under an isolated configured home.

case_workflow.goal: Ensure a custom HERMES_HOME fully isolates one Hermes instance's persistent runtime state from the operating-system home and other instances.

case_actions.action: Inventory persistent and generated runtime paths across CLI, gateway, agent, environment, and tool modules that directly construct ~/.hermes or Path.home()/.hermes instead of using the configured runtime home.

Convert both module-level storage constants and per-operation path construction to use get_hermes_home(), an existing resolved CLI home, or an equivalent HERMES_HOME-aware expression, retaining ~/.hermes as the default when no override is configured.

Configure HERMES_HOME to an isolated temporary directory and exercise representative read and write behaviors, asserting that discovered session state and generated clipboard images are located beneath that configured root.

preconditions: A canonical runtime-home resolver or equivalent environment-aware root expression exists.
The configurable home must preserve the established ~/.hermes fallback when HERMES_HOME is unset.
Affected paths represent runtime state or generated runtime data that should be isolated per configured Hermes home.
failure_modes: Some hardcoded paths remain outside the audit and continue reading or writing under the operating-system home.
Import-time path constants are initialized from Path.home() or expanduser and bypass the configured root.
Tests patch Path.home() rather than HERMES_HOME, so they do not verify the supported configuration contract.
Only read-oriented or only write-oriented routing is tested, leaving the other direction unverified.

skills.title: Separate newline semantics from boundary encoding
skills.summary: Keep core text processing independent of physical newline encoding by representing line breaks canonically or as a constrained policy, then perform the selected LF, CRLF, or platform conversion at the shared file-write boundary. This avoids scattering encoding logic across callers while allowing output to preserve source style or honor explicit configuration.
